title: Respiratory virus surveillance in the WHO African Region Epidemiological Week 31, July 27 to August 2 2026 - WHO | Regional Office for Africa

analysis.time: During week 31, which corresponds to July 27 to August 2 2026, 1,374 specimens were collected, and 1,368 were tested for influenza (N2). The cumulative data from weeks 1 to 31 was also reported (N6).
analysis.location_and_population: The surveillance covered 23 countries in the WHO African Region, including Algeria, Burkina Faso, Cameroon, Côte d’Ivoire, Democratic Republic of the Congo, Ethiopia, Ghana, Kenya, Liberia, Mali, Mauritania, Mauritius, Niger, Nigeria, Senegal, Seychelles, Sierra Leone, South Africa, Togo, Uganda, United Republic of Tanzania, Zambia, and Zimbabwe (N1).
analysis.event: In Epiweek 31, 172 specimens tested positive for influenza virus, with 124 being Influenza A and 48 being Influenza B (N3). Additionally, 45 specimens tested positive for SARS-CoV-2 out of 1,231 processed by 20 laboratories (N5).
analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: The influenza positivity rate was 12.6% (172 positive specimens out of 1,368 tested), with specific subtypes identified: Influenza A (H1N1)pdm09 (n = 21), Influenza A (H3) (n = 95), Influenza A (unable to subtype) (n = 1), Influenza A (subtyping not performed) (n = 7), Influenza B (lineage not determined) (n = 11), and Influenza B (Victoria) (n = 37) (N4). For SARS-CoV-2, the positivity rate was 3.7% (N5).
analysis.response_status_and_uncertainty: The report details the surveillance activities and results, with no mention of specific responses or actions taken (N1, N2, N3, N4, N5).

analysis.brief_en: During the WHO African Region Epidemiological Week 31, which ran from July 27 to August 2, 2026, respiratory virus surveillance was conducted across 23 countries. A total of 1,374 specimens were collected, and 1,368 were tested for influenza, with 172 testing positive (12.6% positivity rate). Of these, 124 were Influenza A and 48 were Influenza B, including subtypes such as Influenza A (H1N1)pdm09 (21 cases), Influenza A (H3) (95 cases), and Influenza B (Victoria) (37 cases). Additionally, 45 specimens tested positive for SARS-CoV-2 out of 1,231 processed by 20 laboratories, indicating a 3.7% positivity rate. The report highlights the ongoing surveillance efforts but does not specify any targeted responses or actions. The cumulative data from weeks 1 to 31 showed 1,245 positive SARS-CoV-2 cases out of 44,465 specimens tested, with a cumulative positivity rate of 2.8%. These findings are part of the broader respiratory virus surveillance in the region.
analysis.summary_en: During the WHO African Region Epidemiological Week 31, which ran from July 27 to August 2, 2026, respiratory virus surveillance was conducted across 23 countries. A total of 1,374 specimens were collected, and 1,368 were tested for influenza, with 172 testing positive (12.6% positivity rate). Of these, 124 were Influenza A and 48 were Influenza B, including subtypes such as Influenza A (H1N1)pdm09 (21 cases), Influenza A (H3) (95 cases), and Influenza B (Victoria) (37 cases). Additionally, 45 specimens tested positive for SARS-CoV-2 out of 1,231 processed by 20 laboratories, indicating a 3.7% positivity rate. The report highlights the ongoing surveillance efforts but does not specify any targeted responses or actions. The cumulative data from weeks 1 to 31 showed 1,245 positive SARS-CoV-2 cases out of 44,465 specimens tested, with a cumulative positivity rate of 2.8%. These findings are part of the broader respiratory virus surveillance in the region.

title: National flu and COVID-19 surveillance report: 10 September 2026 (week 37) - GOV.UK

analysis.time: The report was published on 10 September 2026 and covers surveillance data up to week 36 of 2026 (31 August – 6 September 2026).
analysis.location_and_population: The surveillance covers England and reports on the general population monitored by the UK Health Security Agency.
analysis.event: The UK Health Security Agency’s weekly surveillance report indicates that influenza activity increased and is circulating at baseline levels, while COVID‐19 activity also increased across some indicators; respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) activity remained low and at baseline levels. These findings are based on laboratory and primary‐care surveillance data.
analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: Influenza laboratory positivity rose to a rolling 7‐day rate of 2.8% (up from 2.4%) with 5.6% of week‐35 samples positive (down from 11.7% the prior week). COVID‐19 PCR positivity in hospitals increased to a rolling 7‐day rate of 4.2% (up from 3.4%). RSV positivity remained stable at 0.1%. No explicit risk level is stated beyond the baseline characterisation.
analysis.response_status_and_uncertainty: The data are provisional and may be retrospectively updated; some surveillance thresholds (MEM and MSD) are experimental and subject to revision, with expert opinion used to interpret trends. Ongoing surveillance and reporting continue.

analysis.brief_en: The UK Health Security Agency’s weekly surveillance report released on 10 September 2026 summarises respiratory virus activity in England for the period 31 August to 6 September 2026 (week 36). Influenza activity has risen, with a rolling 7‐day laboratory positivity of 2.8% and 5.6% of samples testing positive in week 35, though this remains at baseline levels. COVID‐19 shows a similar upward trend, with hospital PCR positivity climbing to 4.2% over the same rolling period. RSV activity stays low, with a stable positivity of 0.1%. The report notes that the data are provisional and that some analytical thresholds are experimental, relying on expert interpretation. Surveillance remains ongoing, and figures may be updated as more information becomes available.
analysis.summary_en: The UK Health Security Agency’s weekly surveillance report released on 10 September 2026 summarises respiratory virus activity in England for the period 31 August to 6 September 2026 (week 36). Influenza activity has risen, with a rolling 7‐day laboratory positivity of 2.8% and 5.6% of samples testing positive in week 35, though this remains at baseline levels. COVID‐19 shows a similar upward trend, with hospital PCR positivity climbing to 4.2% over the same rolling period. RSV activity stays low, with a stable positivity of 0.1%. The report notes that the data are provisional and that some analytical thresholds are experimental, relying on expert interpretation. Surveillance remains ongoing, and figures may be updated as more information becomes available.
